target.title: Fix duplicate menu bar items under Icon + Percentage style
target.body:
Fixes #2162.

## Problem

With **Menu bar style = "Icon + Percentage"** and **Display mode = "Percentage"**, frequent usage updates (e.g. active Codex use) spawn duplicate menu bar items — the same provider appears several times (the reporter saw the icon area "repeatedly rebuilt rather than updated in place").

## Root cause

`lazyStatusItem(for:)` has a reuse guard (`if let existing = statusItems[provider] { return existing }`), but on first vend the item was recorded in `statusItems[provider]` **only after `makeStatusItem(…)` returned** — i.e. after `autosaveName` and button configuration. Button/icon-observation setup can **synchronously re-enter** `lazyStatusItem` for the same provider (an icon/usage update landing mid-setup), and in that window `statusItems[provider]` is still `nil`, so the guard misses and a **duplicate** `NSStatusItem` is vended. Under frequent updates this repeats, producing several duplicates.

`statusItems[provider]` is written in exactly one place and only cleared on shutdown, so this creation-time re-entrancy is the only way duplicates can arise.

## Fix

Move vending into a dedicated `StatusItemController+StatusItemVending.swift` extension and register the item **the instant it is created — before any setup or caller callback** — via an `onCreated` hook in `makeStatusItem`. Re-entrant vends during setup then reuse the existing item instead of creating a new one. Small, contained change; the new extension keeps `StatusItemController`'s body under the `type_body_length` limit.

## Verification

- `swift build` — clean.
- `make check` (SwiftFormat + SwiftLint `--strict`) — 0 violations.
- New `StatusItemReuseRegressionTests` — reproduces the mid-vend re-entrancy by firing a usage update at the moment of creation and asserting a single item is reused. **Verified fail-before / pass-after**: with registration ordered after the setup callback the test fails with the exact duplicate symptom (`updatedItem !== vendedItem`); registering first makes it pass. The test drives the real `vendStatusItem` + `updateIcons` path (no bypass/mock), and uses the repo's `menuBarShowsBrandIconWithPercent` + `.percent` config from the issue.
- `make test` — all groups pass **except** `ClaudeOAuthCredentialsStoreCLIStorageOwnershipTests`, which fails identically on clean `main` with this branch stashed (pre-existing, environment-dependent, unrelated to this change).

**On live repro:** the duplication is a creation-time timing race; it isn't reliably forceable in a GUI session on demand, which is why the regression test reproduces it deterministically against the real vending path instead. Happy to walk through a live check — repro config: Menu bar style → Icon + Percentage, Display → Percentage, active Codex use.

No `CHANGELOG` changes.

target.title: Pause blocked background Claude CLI auth probes
target.body:
## Summary

- classify and coalesce `claude auth status --json` probes instead of collapsing every result to `false`
- persist a bounded cooldown after background Auto probes time out (6 hours) or fail (15 minutes), preventing CodexBar's refresh loop from repeatedly launching a CLI process that is blocked on a macOS Keychain dialog
- preserve recovery paths: clean `loggedIn: false` results are not cooled down, user-initiated/explicit CLI fetches and CLI runtime bypass the app-background gate, and a successful CLI fetch clears it

## Root cause and scope

In #2115, packaged-app unified logs identify `/usr/bin/security` as the process requesting `Claude Code-credentials`. That is the delegated Claude CLI path: CodexBar launches `claude auth status --json`, Claude invokes `security`, the modal prompt prevents the preflight from completing, CodexBar times it out after five seconds, and the next background refresh starts the cycle again.

This complements #2137, which guards CodexBar's direct in-process Security.framework read for MCP-only credentials. It does not cover the child-process `/usr/bin/security` requester seen here. #2102 repairs a different missing-credentials-file state, while #1742 introduced the auth-status preflight involved in this loop.

The patch does not read, modify, or delete Keychain credentials and does not alter Claude authentication. The only persisted value is the cooldown expiry timestamp in `UserDefaults`.

## Tests

- `swift test --filter ClaudeCLIAuth`
- `swift test --filter ClaudeBaselineCharacterizationTests`
- `make check`
- `make test` (reaches the unrelated existing `AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` manual-mode failure at line 117; the same failure reproduces with `swift test --filter AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` and is also documented as a current-main baseline in #2137)

Addresses #2115.

Diagnostic evidence: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2115#issuecomment-4966863339

Related: #2137, #2102, #1742

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from successful `users.info` calls but had no pruning — every unique user ID accumulated forever. `channelCache` already bounds at 1024 via `pruneMapToMaxSize`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the current-main `channelCache` pattern for users: LRU touch on read, `pruneMapToMaxSize` on write, cap `SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 2048`, using `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`.

## User Impact

- Long-running Slack monitors no longer retain unbounded user-name cache entries.
- Active users stay resident (LRU touch); oldest entries evict first after the cap.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `305a9c3b49e18d636eb2891f639c68c866128347` (rebased onto current `main`)

### Author disposition (305a9c3b49e1) — credential + CI

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Exposed Slack credentials from earlier proof pastes | **Manually revoked by operator (confirmed).** No token material kept in Evidence or comments. Future proofs: env/credential store only; Evidence lists kind only. |
| `check-dependencies` | Green on this head (exact-head). |
| `check-test-types` / `ci-gate` | Failed on head `305a9c3b49e1`; PR touches only Slack monitor files. Type lane not reproduced locally (resource ceiling). Please treat as CI/gate follow-up if unrelated to these 3 files. |
| Rebase | Tip parent was current at publish; ahead 1 / behind main `3b2d2d523b1b` with **no** `extensions/slack` file conflicts between parent…main. |


### Rank-up / security refresh (`305a9c3b49e1`)

- Rebased onto current `main` `66def08d8329` (single commit, parent=main).
- Local gates: `oxfmt --check` + `oxlint` + `vitest` on touched Slack monitor files — green (11 tests in `context.test.ts`).
- **Credential disposition (P1):** Previously pasted Slack bot/user/app credentials have been **revoked and rotated by the operator**. Evidence below no longer includes kind+suffix or last-N fragments. No secrets in this PR body or new comments.
- Follow-up policy: future proofs use env/credential store only; Evidence lists token **kind** only.



### CI fix (head `fdfd1de3…`)

- Extracted shared `readLruMapEntry` / `writeLruMapEntry` to `extensions/slack/src/monitor/lru-map-cache.ts` so oversized `context.ts` **shrinks** (818→789; LOC ratchet base was 801).
- Removed broken unused `readCachedUser` (infinite self-call); user reads now use `readLruMapEntry(userCache, …)` so LRU recency tests match production.

### Rank-up coverage

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Rebase onto current main | done |
| Supported `pruneMapToMaxSize` (same as channelCache) | done |
| Eviction + LRU-recency unit coverage | done |
| Redacted **successful** `users.info` + bounded-cache runtime evidence | done (transcript below) |
| Rotate previously exposed credentials | operator revoked/rotated exposed credentials; Evidence scrubbed of suffix fragments |

### L1 unit

- `evicts the oldest user name when the bounded user cache fills` (2050 `users.info` calls after refill)
- `keeps a recently re-resolved user while older entries are evicted` (LRU touch)

### L3 live Slack API + cache path (redacted) — 2026-07-13
